text:
Asha Verma: FYI MandrakePay flagged a regression after we applied their LoRA on top of `mandrake-base-multilang-v1`. Outputs in French/DE invoices now swap decimal separators (1.200,50 -> 1,200.50) and sometimes add an extra currency symbol (€€1200). Repro set attached.

Diego Morales: ouch. That smells like a tokenizer / locale-token mapping mismatch. Did the LoRA training use a different tokenizer or normalization step for thousand/decimal separators?

Asha Verma: LoRA artifact: gs://cust-artifacts/mandrakepay/lora/2026-03-22/amt-lora.tar.gz. Base: mandrake-base-multilang-v1-int4. Promptset: internal:/datasets/mandrakepay/invoices-8cases.json. Happens primarily on non-en locales and long-context receipts.

Ken Ito: also possible quantization-induced token-splitting. With int4 the merged adapters can shift logits around tokens that represent punctuation or symbol tokens (e.g., `,` vs `.` vs `€`). We saw similar once with yen-symbol doubling. I'll run a side-by-side: fp16 base+LoRA vs int4 merged.

Priya Nair: I'll kick off a quick evalpack with locale-aware metrics (decimal-correctness, symbol-duplication-rate, token-boundary-shift). eval-bot please? :pray:

eval-bot: quick-eval (run id: qe-3290)
- dataset: mandrakepay-invoice-8cases
- model: mandrake-base-multilang-v1-int4 + lora-20260322
- metrics: decimal-format-correct: 62%, symbol-dup-rate: 12%, token-boundary-shift: 7%

Diego Morales: CLI I ran locally:
```bash
redwood run --model mandrake-base-multilang-v1-int4 \
  --lora gs://cust-artifacts/mandrakepay/lora/2026-03-22/amt-lora.tar.gz \
  --prompts ./invoices-8cases.json --quant int4 --emit-kvtrace
```
Output snippet: `Montant: €€ 1.200,50` and kvtrace shows boundary at token idx 512 -> 513 where locale tokens switch.

Ken Ito: I checked the LoRA training logs — they applied a pretokenized normalization step that maps `.` and `,` differently for some locales (legacy pipeline). The LoRA's adapter weights therefore expect a different token id layout for punctuation. When merged without remap, the embedding deltas align to wrong ids, causing punctuation tokens to be interpreted as numeric tokens in int4 path.

Asha Verma: interesting. So two possible causes: 1) bad merge/remap across vocab variants, 2) quant amplification. Proposed triage plan:
- Rebuild merged checkpoint with `lora-remap --preserve-token-ids` to align embedding indices.
- Run fp16 merged baseline to confirm removal of quant amplification.
- If still present, run an adapter-surgical patch (remap only punctuation token rows, lightweight) and re-eval.

Priya Nair: I'll prepare an evalmatrix for locales (fr,de,en) + ctx-length buckets and run parallel jobs. Also will collect perplexity delta on punctuation tokens.

Diego Morales: I started a quick remap+merge locally and will post exact commands. If remap fixes majority, we should push a rebuild script for the customer and mark their artifact as "remapped-recommended" in our onboarding page.

Ken Ito: another interim mitigation: for Dedicated deployments we can enable the `locale-token-fallback` routing — route those requests to fp16 pools or to remapped variants if available. That buys us SLA time while customer artifacts are rebuilt.

eval-bot: remap-run (id: rem-3290) status: completed.
- remap applied: preserve_token_ids=true, patched_tokens=[",",".","€","$"]
- eval: decimal-format-correct: 93%, symbol-dup-rate: 1%, token-boundary-shift: 1%

Asha Verma: great news. Remap appears to resolve the issue. Next steps:
- Diego: produce a remapped artifact tarball and upload to gs://cust-artifacts/mandrakepay/lora/2026-03-22/remapped-v1.tar.gz
- Priya: add a short customer note with repro, mitigation, and recommended runtime flags (prefer remapped artifact or fp16).
- Ken: add `locale-token-fallback` default to Dedicated runtime for boolean flag `prefer_remapped=true` while we roll this pattern out.

Diego Morales: will do. Uploading now and running full locale-eval. ETA ~30m.

Priya Nair: I'll draft the short KB entry after full eval passes. Thanks team. :tada:
